You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 50d90e8703d421db773dcdfc3e114960d35796a2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Matthew Flatt <mflatt@racket-lang.org>
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2012 13:22:00 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] bug fix for thread improvement

Fixes a bug introduced with c89fa0cda7.
---
 src/racket/src/thread.c | 5 +++++
 1 file changed, 5 insertions(+)

diff --git a/src/racket/src/thread.c b/src/racket/src/thread.c
index dbcbcb9c96..1ef5f75863 100644
--- a/src/racket/src/thread.c
+++ b/src/racket/src/thread.c
@@ -3325,6 +3325,11 @@ Scheme_Object *scheme_call_as_nested_thread(int argc, Scheme_Object *argv[], voi
 
   scheme_current_thread = p;
 
+  if (!p->gc_prep_chain) {
+    p->gc_prep_chain = gc_prep_thread_chain;
+    gc_prep_thread_chain = p;
+  }
+
   if (p != scheme_main_thread)
     scheme_weak_resume_thread(p);
 
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the failure to properly initialize the `gc_prep_chain` for a thread when it was created. This oversight led to issues in managing the garbage collection preparation chain for threads, which could result in improper handling of memory during garbage collection, potentially causing crashes or memory leaks. The patch adds a check to ensure that the `gc_prep_chain` is set up correctly for new threads.
